A KV cache stores the key and value tensors from previous token predictions so the model can reuse them during autoregressive generation without recomputing attention for each step.

It enables efficient inference by avoiding redundant forward passes over stored hidden states, reducing memory bandwidth and latency in large-scale LLM serving.

answer-para2.content: When you send many small prompts to the same model in quick succession, each request forces the GPU to spin up and tear down kernels repeatedly, which wastes time on context‑switching and leads to under‑utilized compute. Batching groups those requests into a single large forward pass: the model processes all inputs together, so the heavy matrix multiplications happen once for many tokens instead of many times for few tokens. This reduces memory traffic, keeps the GPU’s arithmetic units busy longer, and lets you fill the stream with more work per cycle—essentially turning idle cycles into productive ones. The result is higher throughput (more tokens per second) and lower latency because the hardware can amortize its overhead across a batch rather than handling each request individually. For a junior engineer, think of it as “doing chores together” instead of “going to the gym one by one,” which makes the most out of the limited compute resources on the GPU.
